profile_text.body:
Saltillo's website centers on TouchChat, an iOS app the company describes as a communication solution for people who have difficulty speaking with their natural voice. The site says the app offers customizable features and a range of vocabularies, languages, and voices, and that it is built for a variety of communication disorders. It highlights head tracking, which uses facial recognition on newer iPad Pro and iPhone models to follow head and face movements, along with built-in switch scanning and touch access. It also notes iOS Split View, which lets a user run two apps side by side. The site directs visitors to three different TouchChat apps and to the App Store for downloads.

The site also carries service notices: scheduled maintenance that would briefly take the websites offline on June 4 from 9:30-10:00 PM ET, and an outage of phone numbers starting with "800," with local numbers starting in "330" given instead (Main Number: 330-262-1984, Service: 330-262-0845).

TouchChat is tracked as an education and research AI product, with word prediction, used as an AAC app by students with communication needs and by SLPs on device-based platforms. Its price is listed as TouchChat HD $149.99+ on the App Store, drawn from a 2022 state AT program list, so that figure may be out of date. Privacy practices for the app are not verified.
